text: U.S. Department of Justice. Office of the Deputy Attorney General. LIMITED OFFICIAL USE. Associate Deputy Attorney General. Washington, D.C. 20530. MEMORANDUM FOR THE ACTING ATTORNEY GENERAL. THROUGH: Robert K. Hur RKH, Principal Associate Deputy Attorney General. FROM: Scott N. Schools SNS, Associate Deputy Attorney General. SUBJECT: Confirmation of Authorization of the Special Counsel to Investigate Enumerated Matters. TIMETABLE: As soon as possible. SUMMARY: The Special Counsel requests confirmation of his authority to investigate the matters identified below. The requested confirmation facilitates an efficient, full, and thorough investigation of the Russian government's efforts to interfere in the 2016 presidential election. As noted below, it may be appropriate to reassign certain matters identified below to a United States Attorney's Office or Department component at some point in the future. I recommend that you confirm the authority of the Special Counsel to investigate matters identified herein. DISCUSSION: On May 17, 2017, you appointed Robert S. Mueller III as Special Counsel “to ensure a full and thorough investigation of the Russian government's efforts to interfere in the 2016 presidential election,” and specified his investigative and prosecutorial authority. Order No. 3915-2017. Thereafter, on August 2, 2017, you executed a classified memorandum that further identified specific matters included within the Special Counsel's investigative authority. During the course of his investigation of the authorized matters, the Special Counsel has identified additional individuals whose conduct he should investigate in order to fulfill his responsibilities as set forth in the appointment order. Those individuals and the basis for their inclusion within the Special Counsel's investigative purview are more fully described below. I. Individuals whose conduct is directly within the scope of the investigation. The Special Counsel's Office (SCO) has been meeting with the Office of the Deputy Attorney General every other week to provide a briefing on the progress of the investigation. description: Photograph of page 2 of the partially redacted DOJ 'LIMITED OFFICIAL USE' October 2017 Special Counsel scope memorandum, with pink highlighter marks and handwritten margin notes reading 'Cohen', 'Gates', 'Stone', and 'Manafort'. The page discusses confirming the Special Counsel's authority to investigate Michael Cohen, Richard Gates, Roger Stone, and additional redacted names, and Paul Manafort's alleged crimes arising from payments from the Ukrainian government under President Viktor Yanukovych. Bates stamp DOJ-HSGAC20200728-000064 appears at bottom left; several passages are blacked out.
text: LIMITED OFFICIAL USE. of additional individuals other than those named in the classified memorandum should be investigated as part of a full and thorough investigation of the Russian government's efforts to interfere in the 2016 presidential election, including any links and/or coordination between the Russian government and individuals associated with the campaign of President Donald Trump. Confirmation of the authorization to investigate such individuals does not suggest that the Special Counsel has made a determination that any of them has committed a crime. Rather, the Special Counsel has learned information such that further investigation of the pertinent activities of Michael Cohen, Richard Gates, [redacted] Roger Stone, and [redacted] is necessary for the Special Counsel to fulfill his responsibilities under the appointment order. I recommend that you confirm the authority of the Special Counsel to conduct that investigation. II. Individuals who are possibly engaged in jointly undertaken activity pertaining to authorized matters. The Special Counsel has also identified persons or entities who may have been engaged in jointly undertaken activity with individuals the investigation of whom you previously determined to be within the scope of your appointment order. Investigation by the Special Counsel of these additional persons or entities would be consistent with the ordinary course for a United States Attorney's Office or a Department component. In other words, any such office investigating potential criminal activity by one person would include within the same investigation individuals or entities who may have been jointly involved to determine whether they are targets, subjects, or witnesses, or are wholly uninvolved. This practice increases efficiency by avoiding multiple investigations of the same conduct. It also enables the prosecuting office to be aware of the full scope of the conduct to accurately assess the relative culpability of all involved and to identify and obtain the cooperation of co-defendants and witnesses. Assignment at this time of the investigation of persons or entities who may have engaged in jointly undertaken activity to a United States Attorney's Office or Department component would create the possibility that an individual with relevant information about the Special Counsel's investigation might come forward with that information after the Special Counsel concludes his investigation. This occurrence would raise questions about the completeness of the Special Counsel's investigation and the accuracy of his conclusions. Confirmation of the Special Counsel's authority to investigate these matters would not preclude reassignment of such matters to a United States Attorney's Office or Department component at a later time. You previously confirmed the Special Counsel's authority to investigate allegations that Paul Manafort committed a crime or crimes arising out of payments he received from or on behalf of the Ukrainian government before and during the tenure of President Viktor Yanukovych. The Special Counsel has determined that the following individuals or entities may have been jointly involved in that conduct: Richard Gates; [redacted]. I recommend that you confirm the Special Counsel's authority to investigate those individuals and entities in connection with their possible participation in that conduct. 2. LIMITED OFFICIAL USE. DOJ-HSGAC20200728-000064. Cohen. Gates. Stone. Manafort.

description: Photograph of page 3 of the partially redacted DOJ 'LIMITED OFFICIAL USE' October 2017 Special Counsel scope memorandum, resting on a laptop keyboard with pink highlighter marks and a handwritten margin note reading 'Flynn / Business interests'. The page covers allegations that Michael Flynn acted as an unregistered agent of Turkey (with Bijan Rafiekian and Ekim Alptekin possibly jointly involved), a section on Michael Cohen's Essential Consultants LLC and funds from Russian-backed entities, a fully blacked-out Section IV, and the summary recommendation to confirm the Special Counsel's authority. Bates stamp DOJ-HSGAC20200728-000065 appears at bottom left.
text: LIMITED OFFICIAL USE. Flynn / Business interests. You also previously confirmed the Special Counsel's authority to investigate allegations that Michael Flynn committed a crime or crimes by acting as an unregistered agent of Turkey. The Special Counsel has determined that Bijan Rafikian and Ekim Alptekin may have been jointly involved in that conduct. I recommend that you confirm the Special Counsel's authority to investigate those individuals and entities in connection with their possible participation in that conduct. III. Michael Cohen. In the course of the investigation, with respect to Michael Cohen, the Special Counsel has discovered investigative leads the pursuit of which may result in the discovery of criminal conduct not directly related to the Russian government's efforts to interfere in the 2016 presidential election. Those leads relate to Cohen's establishment and use of Essential Consultants LLC in order to, inter alia, receive funds from Russian-backed entities. Because the investigation has also revealed links between Cohen and Russian government officials, the Special Counsel would like to pursue those leads for at least two reasons: (1) there is some evidence that certain of Cohen's actions may relate to the Russian government's efforts to interfere in the 2016 presidential election; and (2) Cohen may have information relevant to the Special Counsel's investigation, and pursuit of the leads may help to secure Cohen's cooperation, thus furthering the Special Counsel's full and thorough investigation of the Russian government's efforts to interfere in the 2016 presidential election. I recommend you confirm the authority of the Special Counsel to pursue the referenced leads. IV. [redacted]. V. Summary recommendation. Based on the briefings the Special Counsel's Office has provided, I believe that the matters over which the Special Counsel seeks to confirm investigative authority are sufficiently predicated and appropriately within the scope of your appointment order. Further, centralizing the investigation of the identified matters with the Special Counsel for the time being will lead to a more timely and credible resolution of the investigation, which is squarely in the Department's and the nation's interests. For these reasons, I recommend you confirm the Special Counsel's authority to investigate the named individuals and matters in addition to those individuals and matters identified in the previously referenced classified memorandum.
